items.title: Iran reaffirms military alliance with Russia as war intensifies

featured_image.name: Minister: Iran to respond forcefully to any 'transgression'

items.description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday dismissed growing international calls for a ceasefire in the country's widening war with the United States and Israel, declaring Tehran will keep fighting until it secures a lasting end to hostilities. The remarks, made during an appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press," came as the conflict entered its second week with no signs of abating and Iran moved closer to naming a successor to the slain Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.[1][2]

"There should be a permanent end of the war. And unless we get to that, I think we need to continue fighting for the sake of our people and our security," Araghchi said. He directly rejected President Trump's demand for Iran's unconditional surrender, drawing a comparison to last year's 12-day conflict with Israel. "We resisted, and after 12 days the Israelis asked for an unconditional ceasefire. So we never give up. We never surrender".[3]

items.title: Trump rebuffs UK carrier readiness, says US 'already won' Iran war

featured_image.name: Keir Starmer channels Top Gun on visit to Britain's flagship aircraft  carrier as PM issues 'new era' warning | The Standard

items.description:
President Donald Trump publicly dismissed Britain's move to ready its aircraft carrier for possible deployment to the Middle East on Saturday, declaring the United States has "already won" its war with Iran and does not need belated help from its closest ally.

"The United Kingdom, our once Great Ally, maybe the Greatest of them all, is finally giving serious thought to sending two aircraft carriers to the Middle East," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "That's OK, Prime Minister Starmer, we don't need them any longer — But we will remember. We don't need people that join Wars after we've already won!"[1][2]

The broadside came shortly after the UK Ministry of Defence announced it had halved the deployment readiness window for HMS Prince of Wales, the Royal Navy's flagship carrier, from 10 days to five, according to Sky News. A British official said no final decision had been made on sending the carrier to the region.[2][3]

items.title: Toxic black rain blankets Tehran after Israeli strikes on oil depots

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Israel hits Tehran oil depots; 2 killed in Saudi Arabia

items.description:
Tehran awoke Sunday morning to an apocalyptic scene: thick black clouds blocking out the sun and oil-saturated rain falling across Iran's capital after Israeli airstrikes destroyed multiple fuel storage facilities overnight. The Iranian Red Crescent issued urgent warnings to the city's residents, saying the fires had released "significant quantities of toxic hydrocarbon compounds, sulfur, and nitrogen oxides" into the atmosphere.[1][2]

"In the event of precipitation, the resulting rain is extremely dangerous and highly acidic," the Red Crescent said in a statement, warning that exposure could cause skin burns and severe lung damage.[3][2]

items.title: Iran threatens to strike regional oil sites after Israel hits Tehran fuel depots

items.description: Iran's military command threatened on Sunday to strike oil facilities across the Middle East if Israel continues its attacks on the Islamic Republic's energy infrastructure, warning that oil prices could surge above $200 per barrel. items.description: The Israeli military announced Sunday that it killed Abu al-Qassem Baba'iyan, the newly appointed head of the military bureau of Iran's supreme leader, in a precision airstrike in Tehran on Saturday. The strike represents the latest in a systematic Israeli campaign to dismantle Iran's senior military command structure since the start of hostilities on February 28.

items.title: Russia says it intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones in four hours

featured_image.name: Russia's drone revolution heaps pressure on Ukrainian ...

items.description:
Russia's Defense Ministry said on Sunday that its air defense units intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones over central and southern Russia within a four-hour window, in what officials described as a higher-than-average wave of aerial attacks that included two drones headed for Moscow.[1][2]

The interceptions took place between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m. Moscow time (1100-1500 GMT), according to the ministry. The Bryansk region, which borders Ukraine, recorded the highest concentration with 73 drones intercepted. No damage or casualties were reported.[3][4]

items.title: US, Israel weigh special forces raid to seize Iran's enriched uranium

items.description: The United States and Israel have discussed sending special forces into Iran to secure its stockpile of highly enriched uranium at a later stage of the ongoing war, Axios reported Saturday, citing four sources with knowledge of the discussions.
